subject: Re: Cedar Peak — increased 5xx & latency from us-west-2, requesting exec bridge
messages:
From: Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@cedar-peak.com>
To: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@cedar-peak.com>, Cedar Peak NOC <noc@cedar-peak.com>
Date: 2028-08-01 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact — high latency and 5xx from us-west-2 starting 07:45 PDT

Michael —

We started seeing a surge of 5xx errors and large tail latency (p95 -> 4.6s) around 07:45 PDT in our US-WEST-2 traffic. This is affecting our checkout flow and is resulting in retries from our side. We opened a ticket with your support portal (INC-6212) but wanted to escalate because we're having to enable degraded-mode fallbacks on our side.

Summary:
- Impact window: ~07:45 PDT -> ongoing
- Error class: 502/504 and occasional 5xx spikes to 2% of requests (baseline ~0.02%)
- Latency: median unchanged, p95/p99 increased sharply
- Traffic: Cedar Peak sends ~45% of traffic to us-west-2, rest routed across regions

Can we get an exec-level bridge and immediate routing guidance? We cannot keep degraded-mode in place for long.

Attaching a small set of our client-side logs.

Thanks,
Julia Ramos
Director, Platform Engineering
Cedar Peak
[attachment: cedar_client_errs_0801.log (txt, 220KB)]

From: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-01 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — high latency and 5xx from us-west-2 starting 07:45 PDT

Hi Julia —

Thank you for the alert and the logs. I'm sorry for the disruption. I've bumped this to P0 internally and asked our SRE team to stand up a bridge. Marissa is looped for customer comms and Sean for commercial/exec escalation.

Immediate next steps we are taking:
- SRE (Stephanie) is pulling system-side logs and metrics now; we will share an initial incident timeline within 15 minutes.
- We'll evaluate emergency cross-region redistribution to us-west-1/us-east-1 for your traffic and propose a safe cutover plan.
- If safe, we can pin a fallback model variant (lower-memory quantized model) for Cedar Peak to reduce KV-cache pressure while we diagnose.

Can you confirm the window Cedar Peak can tolerate a 30–60s API DNS/route shift? Also please share any downstream timeouts you have (client retry policy) so we can avoid retry storms during cutover.

I'll send the bridge link in the next update.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
[attachment: INC-6212_customer_logs_bundle.txt (brief)]

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-01 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — high latency and 5xx from us-west-2 starting 07:45 PDT

On 01 Aug 2028 08:28, michael_grant@redwood.ai wrote:
> I'll send the bridge link in the next update.

Bridge is up: https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/INC-6212 (pin code on bridge).

Preliminary findings (first 20m):
- We saw an intra-AZ autoscaler oscillation in us-west-2's GPU pool starting 07:40 PDT; nodes terminated and reattached frequently, causing ephemeral KV-cache misses and increased cold-start latencies.
- Error pattern correlates with a burst of longer sequences (avg token length +120% for Cedar Peak) which amplified memory pressure.
- No immediate signs of network fabric outage, NICs look healthy; this appears to be scheduling / capacity churn.

Triage actions in progress:
1) Temporarily suspend aggressive autoscale down in the affected us-west-2 pool (already applied).
2) Start live redispatch for Cedar Peak's production route to prefer us-west-1 (warm path) with gradual 10% increments every 60s.
3) Pin Cedar Peak's route to the quantized-8bit model variant (less memory) as a fallback during redispatch.
4) Collect a packaged log bundle for you (cedar_peak_logs_usw2_0801.zip) and a token-level slo chart.

Ask for you all: please confirm if Cedar Peak can accept a phased 10%/min traffic shift. If not, we can accelerate to 50% but will need client-side retry coordination.

Stephanie Nguyen
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: runbook_usw2_az_drill.pdf (stub)]

From: Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@cedar-peak.com>
To: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@cedar-peak.com>, Cedar Peak NOC <noc@cedar-peak.com>
Date: 2028-08-01 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — high latency and 5xx from us-west-2 starting 07:45 PDT

Thanks — we can accept a phased shift at 10%/min. Our checkout timeout is 10s and clients retry after exponential backoff; please avoid spikes that would trigger client retries above 10%.

Also, our exec team is on standby and has asked for an estimated recovery time and any customer impact window to share with operations. Can you confirm if this is limited to Cedar Peak or if other customers in us-west-2 are impacted?

Julia

On a related note — if this results in SLA credits, please advise on next steps; we will open a formal credit request after incident closes.

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@cedar-peak.com>
Date: 2028-08-01 13:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — high latency and 5xx from us-west-2 starting 07:45 PDT

Quick update after the bridge and remediation:

What we did:
- Rolled phased traffic from us-west-2 -> us-west-1 at 10%/min starting 08:45 PDT; completed a 70% redistribution by 09:12 PDT.
- Pinned Cedar Peak's route to quantized-8bit variant for 2 hours to lower memory pressure and KV cache churn.
- Stabilized the us-west-2 autoscaler: disabled scale-down threshold that was too aggressive and applied a 5m stabilization window.

Impact & outcome:
- 5xx rate for Cedar Peak dropped from 2% -> 0.06% within 18 minutes of shift.
- p95 latency returned close to baseline by 09:10 PDT for shifted traffic; residual latency remained for small portion still on us-west-2.
- Other customers: No broad region-wide outage observed; impact appears concentrated to pools with high long-sequence workload patterns (Cedar Peak being the most severe).

Next steps (post-incident):
- SRE will perform a root-cause postmortem and share within 48 hours (INC-6212).
- Support will open a formal SLA review and provide guidance on credit process (Marissa).
- Propose a scheduled capacity hardening window next week to prevent autoscaler oscillation during peak token-length bursts.

Marissa — can you coordinate the credit request and exec summary for Cedar Peak? Michael — please coordinate any commercial asks. Julia — appreciate the patience; we'll follow up with the PM/Eng postmortem and a runbook change log.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Success (Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference
